title: How much longer does an even match take?

prereqs.why: The expected duration of the fair game is the formula being applied twice.
The set-up is the same two-barrier walk; only the quantity being computed changes.

statement:
A gambler plays independent **fair** $\pounds1$ games, stopping when her
wealth reaches $\pounds 0$ or $\pounds 100$.

Conditioning on the first game gives $t_k = 1 + \tfrac12 t_{k+1} + \tfrac12 t_{k-1}$
with $t_0 = t_{100} = 0$, whose solution is

$$t_k = k\,(m - k), \qquad m = 100 .$$

**Session A** starts with $\pounds 30$. **Session B** starts with $\pounds 50$.

Give $\;\E(\text{games in session B}) - \E(\text{games in session A})$.
hints: Work out $t_{30}$ and $t_{50}$ separately from the formula and subtract.
$t_{30} = 30 \times 70$ and $t_{50} = 50 \times 50$. Both are larger than most people expect.
The function $k \mapsto k(m-k)$ is a downward parabola with its maximum at $k = m/2$, so session B is the longest possible session for this target.

payload.prompt: The difference in expected number of games.
payload.label: $t_{50} - t_{30} =$
payload.syntax: A whole number. Arithmetic is fine: 2500-2100 is read as 400.
